Maia for Metrics digests

Post the metric with its definition.

Maia turns approved metric outputs into a short, readable digest. Each result keeps its reporting period, definition, and source freshness in view.

All use cases ↗

Start with approved outputs

A digest should communicate metrics, not create a shadow analytics system. Supply approved metric outputs, the metric dictionary, reporting periods, and freshness timestamps. If a figure comes from an export, identify when it was produced.

Ask Maia to preserve definitions and denominators. A percentage without its cohort or period can mislead even when the arithmetic is correct.

Build a readable digest

Maia can group metrics by business question, compare them with the prior period, and flag exceptions. It can include a short explanation when the supplied records support one.

The digest should link to its sources and mark stale or missing inputs. Maia should not infer a cause from correlation alone.

Limit the digest to metrics that serve a defined audience. A leadership update and a growth review may use the same source but need different detail. Supply the audience and the decisions they own.

Review in the analytics channel

An analyst checks formulas, periods, signs, and definitions before the digest reaches a wider audience. Teammates can ask follow-up questions in the thread, while Maia keeps the original definition beside the answer.

A practical example

The approved export reports 41% activation for one cohort. The dictionary shows that activation changed from a seven-day to a fourteen-day window. Maia flags the definition change instead of presenting the movement as a product effect. It also notes that support data is one day older than revenue data.

The analyst confirms the period and approves the digest.

Schedule with care

A routine can prepare the digest after the approved output arrives. Include a freshness rule so Maia stops or warns when a source has not updated. Scheduling a prompt does not make an upstream metric reliable.

Keep the previous digest for comparison, but do not silently reuse its values. Each run should state its own period and source time. If a definition changes, show the break rather than drawing one trend across unlike measures.

Give readers a path to the detailed source. The Slack digest should support a decision, while the approved report retains the full breakdown and methodology.

Common questions

Can Maia calculate metrics?

It can work with supplied data and formulas, but an analyst should validate calculations and definitions.

Can Maia query our warehouse?

Only through a verified, authorized connection. This workflow also works with approved exports.

How should missing data appear?

Show the missing period or source plainly. Do not silently carry forward an old value.
